data.name: Hint
data.value: What the company pays you for the rights on works you create, code, a game or content, which you transfer or license to it. Within the limits it stays movable income: the company deducts it in full and withholds 15%, and you are taxed on it apart at 15% plus your municipal surcharge, with no social contributions. What passes the limits is taxed as your pay.

data.name: AverageHint
data.value: The royalty stays within its limits only while your copyright income of the four previous years, counted before those limits, averaged at most the year's cap. Netto cannot see it, so it assumes it did until you say otherwise. When it did not, Netto taxes the whole royalty as your pay: the law makes the average a condition without saying more, and that reading never overstates the gain.

data.value: Where no text settles a point, Netto takes the reading that never overstates the gain: the 30% is measured on your gross pay on the payslip alone, without benefits in kind or the contributions the company pays for you; neither the royalty nor its part taxed as pay counts in the {0} minimum pay that keeps the reduced corporate rate; and the royalty is always taxed apart, never with your other income.
